name: Kanban update
input: Status event from an agent: item ID, from-column, to-column, evidence file path
steps: 1 Read the event. 2 Check the exit criteria for the current column (stage gate check). 3 If all pass, move the item and add one History row. 4 If a human gate applies, write 'Awaiting approval: <role>' and do not move. 5 Commit: kanban: <ID> <from> → <to>
output: Updated kanban.md with one new History row
verification: Every move has one History row with evidence path

name: Kanban consistency check
steps: 1 Check each item appears in one column only. 2 Check every move has a History row. 3 Check each 'Awaiting approval' has a matching checkpoint file
output: Consistency report listing violations (empty if none)
verification: Report has zero violations or lists each one

name: Stage gate check
input: Item ID, current column, exit criteria (from kanban.md Columns table), evidence files
steps: 1 Read the exit criteria for the column. 2 Find evidence for each criterion. 3 Mark each criterion pass or fail with the evidence path. 4 Return the result to A1.01
output: Gate result table: criterion, pass/fail, evidence path
verification: Each criterion has pass/fail and an evidence path

name: Work item routing
input: Item in Backlog or Ready, with its type (story, task, bug)
steps: 1 Read item type. 2 Look up the next agent in the agent table. 3 Write the handoff request
output: Routing decision: next agent and reason
verification: Routing matches the agent table in .github/sdlc/config.yml

name: Checkpoint manager
input: Any agent request that needs a human decision (decision request or gate)
steps: 1 Create docs/sdlc/checkpoints/CP-xx-<name>.md from the template. 2 Fill: what to decide, options, evidence, default if PROPOSED. 3 Set status OPEN. 4 Block the item in kanban.md. 5 Record the human decision with name and date when given. Never set status APPROVED yourself
output: Checkpoint file with status OPEN, APPROVED or REJECTED
verification: Status is set only by a named human; no agent sets APPROVED

name: Handoff recorder
input: Output of a finished agent step and its verification result (S.04)
steps: 1 Check the verification result is PASS. 2 Write the handoff file: from, to, input files, output files, open checkpoints. 3 Add the handoff path to the item in kanban.md
output: Handoff file linking input and output files
verification: Every output file listed exists at its path

name: Board status report
steps: 1 Count items per column. 2 List blocked items and items awaiting a checkpoint. 3 Name the bottleneck column
verification: Counts add up to the total items on the board

name: Flow metrics
steps: 1 Compute lead time (Backlog to Done). 2 Compute cycle time (In Progress to Done). 3 Compute throughput per week
verification: Each metric shows its formula and row count used

name: Daily standup summary
input: docs/sdlc/kanban.md and the last day of handoff files
steps: 1 Group items by done, in progress, blocked. 2 List the agent that holds each item
verification: Every item on the board appears once

name: Retrospective facilitation
input: Flow metrics, blocked items, fix-loop counts from A8.04
steps: 1 Collect cycle time, blockers, defects. 2 Draft three questions per topic. 3 Leave decisions to the team
verification: Every point cites a metric or a file

name: Sprint planning support
input: Ready items and capacity (TBD if not given)
steps: 1 List Ready items. 2 Show capacity figures, TBD where not given. 3 Propose two sprint goal options
output: Sprint options for a human to choose
verification: Every option lists the items it includes

name: Project bootstrap
input: .github/sdlc/config.yml (filled by a human) and an empty docs/sdlc/
steps: 1 Read config.yml; stop and list every key under required: that is missing or TBD. 2 Create docs/sdlc/ with kanban.md (Columns table from config.yml kanban.columns), inputs/, stories/, design/, architecture/, build/, tests/, review/, release/, checkpoints/, handoffs/, logs/. 3 Write a README in docs/sdlc/ naming the first prompt to run. 4 Commit: sdlc: bootstrap
output: docs/sdlc/ tree and an empty kanban.md with the Columns table
verification: Every folder in the Folder Tree sheet exists; kanban.md has 8 columns

name: Input intake and type detection
input: Raw input in docs/sdlc/inputs/<ID>/: text story, epic text, screenshot files (PNG/JPG), Figma link (phase 2)
steps: 1 List every input file or link. 2 Assign an ID: T-01 text, SS-01 screenshot, FIG-01 Figma. 3 Detect type: story, epic, screenshot, Figma, mixed. 4 Write the manifest
output: Input manifest: ID, type, file path, date received
verification: Every input has an ID, type and file path

name: Epic decomposition
steps: 1 Read the epic. 2 Split into features by user goal. 3 Give each feature an ID (US-001…). 4 List features that the epic does not state as TBD
output: Feature list with IDs and source reference
verification: Every feature cites a sentence of the epic

name: User story writing
input: Feature list or story text from the manifest
steps: 1 Write each story as: As a <role>, I want <goal>, so that <benefit>. 2 Use only roles and goals in the source. 3 Mark any missing role or benefit TBD
output: User stories with IDs and source IDs
verification: Every story has role, goal and benefit, or TBD

name: Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then)
steps: 1 For each story write 2-5 Given/When/Then criteria. 2 Each criterion has one observable result. 3 Note platform differences where the source states them. 4 Mark unknown results TBD
verification: Each criterion has one observable result; no 'should work well'

name: Platform and scope definition
steps: 1 List target platform: web, mobile, or both. 2 List browsers or OS versions only if the source states them. 3 Write the in-scope and out-of-scope list. 4 Mark gaps TBD
output: Scope statement with in-scope and out-of-scope lists
verification: Every platform line states its source or TBD

name: Screenshot screen inventory
steps: 1 Open each screenshot. 2 Name each screen and region with an ID (SS-01-R1). 3 List visible text, buttons, inputs and navigation. 4 Mark values read from pixels as estimated
output: Screen inventory: screen ID, region IDs, visible text, controls
verification: Every screen has a screenshot region ID; estimates are labelled

name: UX state definition
steps: 1 For each screen check loading, empty, error, offline, permission-denied. 2 Write the state text the source gives. 3 Mark unknown states TBD and add a checkpoint entry
verification: Every screen has all five states, each stated or TBD

name: UX spec writing
steps: 1 Write one section per screen: purpose, controls, flow to next screen. 2 Leave design choices the source does not make as TBD. 3 Cite the source for each line
verification: No line without a source ID or TBD

name: Definition of Ready check
input: Stories, criteria, scope, UX spec, checkpoint log (S.02)
steps: 1 Check each story against the Definition of Ready in .github/sdlc/config.yml. 2 Record pass or fail per story with evidence. 3 If any CP-07 for this item is not APPROVED, mark the check FAIL, list the open CP-07 files, and stop; do not request CP-01. 4 If all pass, request CP-01 through A1.05
output: Ready report: story, check, pass/fail, evidence
verification: Every story has a pass or fail result with evidence

name: Clarifying question and checkpoint builder
input: Any TBD found by A2 skills
steps: 1 List each TBD with the file and line it appears in. 2 Write the question with 2-3 options. 3 Send each to A1.05 as a checkpoint
verification: Every TBD in the stories folder has one checkpoint entry

name: Scope check against input
steps: 1 Map each story to an input ID. 2 Flag any story without a source. 3 Move suggested extra features to a decision request (S.03), not into scope
output: Scope check table: story, input ID, status
verification: Every story has an input ID or a flag

name: NFR capture
input: Stories and any non-functional requirements in the source
steps: 1 List performance, offline, accessibility, size and battery needs stated in the source. 2 Mark each unstated value TBD
verification: Every NFR cites its source or TBD

name: Privacy and data requirement capture
steps: 1 List personal data fields the stories name. 2 List permissions and consent the stories imply. 3 Mark the rest TBD
verification: Each personal data field cites a story

name: Figma design read
input: Figma link or file (read access granted at CP-08)
steps: 1 Read frames and components via the Figma connector. 2 Record each screen with its node ID. 3 Record text and component names exactly. 4 Stop and report if access is denied
output: Figma inventory: screen, node ID, components, text
verification: Every screen has a Figma node ID

name: Figma vs story gap check
input: Stories and Figma or screenshot inventory
steps: 1 Compare each story with the screens. 2 List screens with no story, and stories with no screen. 3 Cite both IDs
output: Gap list citing story and screen IDs
verification: Each gap cites both IDs

name: Edge case and glossary extraction
steps: 1 List edge cases stated or implied by the source. 2 List domain terms with the source sentence. 3 Log unclear terms
verification: Each term has a source sentence

name: Text-only UX baseline (PROPOSED)
input: Approved stories and UX spec (no screenshot or Figma)
steps: 1 Derive user journeys from the stories. 2 List screens and navigation between them. 3 Define screen states. 4 Label everything PROPOSED with a reason
verification: Every screen traces to a story; every item is labelled PROPOSED

name: Screenshot design extraction
steps: 1 Read colours, font sizes, spacing and radius from each screenshot. 2 Record each value as estimated. 3 Group values into candidate tokens
output: Extracted design values, all marked estimated
verification: Every value is marked estimated and cites a region ID

name: Baseline UI layout plan
input: UI baseline or extracted design, screen inventory
steps: 1 For each screen write a text wireframe: regions, primary action, order of content. 2 Confirm one primary action per screen. 3 Label PROPOSED where the source is silent
verification: Each screen has exactly one primary action

name: Design tokens (extracted or PROPOSED)
input: Extracted design values (A3.02) or PROPOSED defaults
steps: 1 Set colour, type scale, spacing and radius tokens. 2 Give each token a reason or source. 3 Check text contrast against 4.5:1 with a tool. 4 Save as JSON
output: tokens.json with reason and source per token
verification: Every text colour pair passes 4.5:1 per the tool output

name: Component spec writer
steps: 1 List each component on each screen. 2 For each, write props, states, variants and sizes. 3 Refer to tokens by name only
verification: Each component lists its states

name: Responsive layout rules
input: Layout plan and platform scope from A2.05
steps: 1 Define a rule for each supported width (web) or screen size and orientation (mobile). 2 Define safe areas and text scaling. 3 Mark sizes not in scope TBD
verification: Each screen has a rule for each supported size

name: Design system bootstrap
input: tokens.json and component specs; existing theme file if any
steps: 1 Check for an existing theme file. 2 Draft the theme file from tokens. 3 Mark it NOT ADOPTED. 4 Request CP-02 through A4.10
output: Draft theme file, marked NOT ADOPTED
verification: File carries NOT ADOPTED until a named approval is recorded

name: UX heuristics review
steps: 1 Check visibility of status, error prevention, consistency and feedback. 2 List each violation with the screen ID
verification: Each violation cites a screen ID

name: Design source replacement
input: PROPOSED baseline and a new Figma or screenshot source
steps: 1 Compare each new source screen with the baseline. 2 Replace PROPOSED values with source values. 3 Log every difference
output: Updated design and a difference log
verification: Every changed value appears in the difference log

name: Figma design extraction
steps: 1 Read colour, type, spacing and elevation with node IDs. 2 Record each value with its node ID. 3 Build tokens from the values
verification: Every value cites a node ID

name: Design system mapping to existing components
input: Figma components and existing project components
steps: 1 Match each Figma component to a project component. 2 List unmatched items. 3 Log unmatched items as checkpoint entries
output: Mapping table with matched and unmatched rows
verification: Every Figma component is matched or logged

name: Asset mapping
steps: 1 List each icon and image with its node ID. 2 Assign a file name and export density
output: Asset list with names and densities
verification: Every asset has a node ID and a file name

name: Accessibility annotations extract
input: Design file or screenshot, component specs
steps: 1 Extract labels, roles, reading order and contrast notes. 2 Mark any value read from pixels as estimated
verification: Each annotation cites a screen or node ID

name: ADR writing
input: Decision question and candidate options from the design or stack analysis
steps: 1 Write context. 2 List at least two options with pros and cons. 3 Write the decision as PROPOSED. 4 Add consequences. 5 Leave the status as PROPOSED until a named person approves
verification: ADR has two or more options and consequences

name: Stack selection analysis
input: Stories, NFRs, platform scope, team skills (TBD if not given)
steps: 1 List candidate frameworks for web and for mobile (React Native or Flutter if mobile). 2 Compare against needs. 3 Mark missing team data TBD. 4 Write the ADR through A4.01
verification: Every comparison cell cites a source or TBD

name: Application architecture design
steps: 1 Define layers: UI, state, API client, backend services, data. 2 Define module boundaries. 3 Define error and logging approach
output: Architecture description with a layer diagram in text
verification: Each module has one owner

name: Data model design
steps: 1 List entities named in stories. 2 List fields, types and keys only where stated. 3 Mark other fields TBD. 4 Map entity relationships
output: Entity list with fields, keys and relationships
verification: Every entity cites a story or is marked TBD

name: API contract design (OpenAPI)
input: Data model, user flows from the UX spec
steps: 1 List endpoints required by each flow. 2 Write request and response schemas. 3 Define error responses. 4 Save as OpenAPI 3
verification: Contract passes the linter (A6.06)

name: Navigation and flow design
steps: 1 Map each screen to a stack, tab or modal (mobile) or route (web). 2 Define entry and exit points. 3 List deep links only if the source states them
verification: Every screen appears once in the map

name: Repository structure plan
steps: 1 Propose folders for frontend, backend, tests, deploy. 2 Check against the team template if one is set in config. 3 Mark missing template TBD
verification: Template check passes, or TBD is logged

name: Design doc writer
input: ADRs, navigation, API contract, data model, UI baseline
steps: 1 Collect the approved parts. 2 Write one design doc with a section per part. 3 Add a section of TBD items
verification: Every section cites its source file

name: Task breakdown
steps: 1 Split the design into tasks sized for one PR. 2 Give each task a frontend, backend or test scope. 3 Link each task to its story ID
verification: Every story maps to at least one task

name: Design approval request
steps: 1 Write the approval request: what to approve, evidence paths, open TBDs. 2 Send to A1.05. 3 Stop until the named approver answers
output: Approval request for CP-02 or CP-03
verification: Request lists every file the approver must read

name: Security architecture review
steps: 1 Check where secrets are stored. 2 Check transport security and auth flows. 3 List each risk with the file it affects
verification: Each finding cites a file

name: Performance budget definition
steps: 1 Propose startup, response-time and bundle-size targets as PROPOSED. 2 Give a reason for each. 3 Leave confirmation to a human
verification: Every value is PROPOSED with a reason

name: Third-party dependency evaluation
steps: 1 Check maintenance activity, licence, size and known vulnerabilities for each library. 2 Record the source of each fact
verification: Each fact cites a source

name: Offline and sync design
steps: 1 Define local storage and cache rules. 2 Define conflict resolution. 3 Mark anything not stated TBD
verification: Every rule cites a requirement or TBD

name: Native boundary decision (mobile)
steps: 1 List features that need native code. 2 Give trade-offs for each. 3 Request a human decision
verification: Each option lists a trade-off

name: Task plan
input: One task from A4.09 with its story and design files
steps: 1 List files to create or change. 2 List tests to write. 3 List risks. 4 Save the plan before coding
verification: Plan lists every file the PR changes

name: Component codegen from spec
steps: 1 Create each component from its spec. 2 Use tokens by name only. 3 Implement every listed state
verification: No colour, size or spacing value is hard-coded outside tokens

name: Screen implementation
input: Layout plan, navigation map, UX spec and states
steps: 1 Build each screen from its layout plan. 2 Implement loading, empty, error and permission-denied states. 3 Use the navigation map for routes
verification: Each screen implements every state from A2.07

name: State and navigation management
input: Architecture ADR for state and routing
steps: 1 Apply the chosen state pattern from the ADR. 2 Apply the chosen routing pattern. 3 Do not mix patterns
verification: Lint rule set from config shows no mixed pattern

name: API wiring
steps: 1 Call only endpoints in the contract. 2 Map each response to the UI state. 3 Map each error to the error state. 4 Add no behaviour beyond the story
verification: Every call matches an operation in openapi.yaml

name: Frontend build configuration
input: Stack from the ADR, environment variable list
steps: 1 Set build tool settings for the stack. 2 Add env variable names with no values. 3 Run the build
verification: Build succeeds on a clean checkout

name: Accessibility implementation
input: Accessibility annotations (A3.13) and minimum UI/UX checklist (S.10)
steps: 1 Add labels and roles to every control. 2 Add focus order. 3 Check contrast uses tokens. 4 Support text scaling
verification: Checklist S.10 items pass for each built screen

name: Platform-specific code handling
steps: 1 Handle browser differences or iOS and Android differences. 2 Isolate platform code in one module per platform. 3 Record each difference
output: Platform modules and a difference list
verification: Every platform branch has a test

name: Dev log writer
input: Changes in the PR and open TBDs
steps: 1 Write what changed and why. 2 List TBDs touched. 3 Link the task ID
verification: Dev log lists every changed file

name: Refactoring and tech debt fixes
input: Tech debt list from the retro or the board
steps: 1 Pick one item in scope. 2 Change structure only. 3 Run the existing tests
verification: Tests pass before and after the change

name: Localization and error text
input: Strings used in the UI and the source of translations (TBD if not given)
steps: 1 Move strings to a resource file. 2 Add keys. 3 Leave translations TBD if not given
verification: Every UI string uses a key

name: Data model and migrations
steps: 1 Write a migration per entity. 2 Add keys and constraints from the data model. 3 Run the migration on an empty database
verification: Migration runs on an empty database with no error

name: API endpoint implementation
steps: 1 Implement each operation in the contract. 2 Validate input. 3 Return the contract error shape
verification: Each handler matches its contract operation

name: Validation and error responses
input: Contract error schema and validation rules from stories
steps: 1 Validate each field against the story rule. 2 Return the contract error for each failure. 3 Log no personal data
verification: Each rule has a test that fails on bad input

name: Auth and authorization
input: Stories that require sign-in and the security review (A4.11)
steps: 1 Implement only the auth flows the stories name. 2 Store secrets outside code. 3 Check permissions on every protected route
verification: Every protected route has a test for denied access

name: Mock data generation
steps: 1 Generate rows that match the model. 2 Label every row SYNTHETIC. 3 Use no real personal data
verification: Every seed file has a SYNTHETIC label

name: API contract validator
steps: 1 Run the OpenAPI linter on the contract. 2 Call each endpoint with a test request. 3 Compare each response with its schema
verification: Linter and response checks both pass

name: Backend environment config and seed
input: Environment variable names and seed data
steps: 1 List variable names with no values. 2 Add a template env file with placeholders. 3 Add a seed script for synthetic data
verification: Template holds no real values; seed script runs

name: Backend container and deploy config
input: Backend build and env variable names
steps: 1 Write a Dockerfile for the backend. 2 Write deploy config with secret references only. 3 Build the image locally
verification: Image builds; no secret value appears in any file

name: BFF layer design
steps: 1 Map each screen's data needs to one BFF endpoint. 2 Define the response shape per screen. 3 List backend calls per endpoint
verification: Every screen maps to one BFF endpoint

name: BFF implementation
steps: 1 Implement each BFF endpoint from the spec. 2 Call backend services. 3 Map errors to the screen error shape
verification: Each BFF endpoint has a contract test

name: External service integration
input: External service names and contracts from the ADR
steps: 1 Write a client per service. 2 Set timeouts and retries as PROPOSED. 3 Map service errors
verification: Each client has a test with a fake service

name: Test plan creation
steps: 1 List the scope from stories. 2 List test types per story. 3 List environments and data. 4 List risks
verification: Every acceptance criterion is in scope

name: Unit test writing
steps: 1 Write a test for each branch and state. 2 Use the test runner in config. 3 Run the tests
verification: Tests pass in the task gate (S.07)

name: Component testing
steps: 1 Render each component alone. 2 Test each listed state. 3 Test each label and role
verification: Each state has a test

name: Integration testing
input: API contract, data model, running backend
steps: 1 Test each endpoint with real storage in a test database. 2 Test error paths. 3 Test the wiring from API client to screen
verification: Each operation has a passing test and each error has one

name: End-to-end test scripting (web)
input: User flows from the UX spec and navigation map
steps: 1 Script each flow from the story. 2 Use a real browser. 3 Assert the visible result from the acceptance criterion
verification: Every acceptance criterion with a flow has a passing E2E test

name: Requirement-to-test traceability
steps: 1 Map each criterion to test IDs. 2 Flag criteria with no test. 3 Record the map
verification: Zero criteria without a test or a flag

name: Defect report writing
input: A failed test with its log
steps: 1 Write steps to reproduce. 2 Record environment, logs and severity. 3 Send to A1.05 as a BUG item
verification: Steps reproduce the failure

name: Test results writer
steps: 1 Count passed, failed, skipped. 2 Link each failure to a defect. 3 Write the report
verification: Totals match the runner output

name: Quality gate summary
input: Test plan, traceability, results, coverage, defects
steps: 1 Summarise results, coverage, open defects. 2 List open risks. 3 Request CP-04 GO or NO-GO from the named approver. 4 Do not record the decision
verification: Summary cites each figure to its file

name: Coverage analysis
input: Coverage report from the test runner
steps: 1 Read line and branch coverage. 2 List untested critical paths. 3 Compare with the threshold in config
verification: Each critical path is listed as tested or not

name: Accessibility testing
steps: 1 Check screen reader labels. 2 Check focus order. 3 Check contrast and target size
verification: Each check states pass or fail with a screen ID

name: Test execution and flaky-test handling
steps: 1 Run the suite several times. 2 Mark a test flaky if results differ. 3 Quarantine it with a defect
verification: Quarantined tests each have a defect ID

name: Regression suite maintenance
input: Code changes and failing tests after the change
steps: 1 List tests the change affects. 2 Update them. 3 Remove none without a note
verification: Suite passes after update

name: Device and browser matrix planning
steps: 1 List browsers or devices in scope. 2 Give the test order. 3 Mark unlisted devices TBD
verification: Every in-scope item has a row

name: Performance testing
steps: 1 Measure each budgeted metric. 2 Compare with the budget. 3 Report each result
verification: Each budget has a measured value

name: Visual regression
steps: 1 Take a screenshot of each screen. 2 Compare with the approved baseline. 3 Send each diff to a human
verification: Each diff is listed for human review

name: PR code review
steps: 1 Read the diff. 2 Check logic, naming and convention rules. 3 Write each comment with its file and line
verification: Every comment cites a file and line

name: Review summary with severity
steps: 1 Group each finding as blocker, major, minor or nit. 2 Write the summary count
verification: Every finding has a severity

name: Review checklist enforcement
input: PR checklist and review checklist from config
steps: 1 Check each checklist item. 2 Mark present or missing. 3 Block the PR if a required item is missing
verification: Every item is marked present or missing

name: Defect fix loop
steps: 1 Send findings to the developer. 2 Re-review the fix. 3 Count each loop. 4 At the limit in config, request CP-06 from a human
verification: Loop count never exceeds the config limit

name: Secrets and credential scan
steps: 1 Run the secret scanner on the diff and config. 2 List each hit by file and line. 3 Block the PR on any hit
verification: Scanner output is attached; zero hits or blocked

name: UI and design standards review
steps: 1 Check colours and sizes come from tokens. 2 Check each component follows its spec. 3 List each deviation
verification: Every deviation cites a file and a spec line

name: CI pipeline configuration
steps: 1 Write a workflow for lint, test and build on each PR. 2 Use secrets references only. 3 Run it on a test PR
verification: Workflow passes on the test PR

name: Build and deploy automation
input: Build config, deploy config, environment names
steps: 1 Write the build step. 2 Write the deploy step with secret references. 3 Run a dry-run deploy
verification: Dry-run deploy passes

name: Versioning and changelog
input: Merged PRs since the last release
steps: 1 Choose the version bump from change types. 2 Write changelog entries from PR titles. 3 Link each entry to its PR
verification: Every entry links to a PR

name: Release checklist
input: Quality summary (CP-04 GO), security results, changelog, deploy config
steps: 1 Check each item: tests green, CP-04 GO recorded, secrets scan clean, config reviewed, rollback plan written. 2 Mark evidence per item. 3 Request CP-05 from the named approver
verification: Every item has evidence; the agent does not approve

name: Review consolidation
steps: 1 Merge findings. 2 Remove duplicates. 3 Keep the highest severity
verification: No duplicate finding remains

name: Security review (OWASP ASVS / MASVS)
steps: 1 Check input handling, storage, auth and transport against ASVS (web) or MASVS (mobile). 2 List each finding with the file
verification: Each finding cites an ASVS or MASVS item

name: Dependency vulnerability check
steps: 1 Run the dependency audit tool. 2 List each advisory and licence issue
verification: Tool output is attached

name: Privacy and PII in logs review
steps: 1 Find each log or analytics call with personal fields. 2 List each with its file and line
verification: Each finding cites a file and line

name: Architecture conformance review
steps: 1 Compare module layout with the architecture doc. 2 List each deviation
verification: Each deviation cites an ADR section

name: Accessibility review
steps: 1 Check labels, focus order, contrast and target size in code. 2 List each finding
verification: Each finding cites a file

name: Crash and release monitoring setup
input: Release target and monitoring tool choice (TBD if not set)
steps: 1 Add the crash reporter config. 2 Add env variable names only. 3 Test one crash event in staging
verification: One test event appears in the tool

name: Staged rollout and rollback plan
steps: 1 Set rollout percentages as PROPOSED. 2 Write rollback steps. 3 Request CP-05 with the plan
verification: Every step names an owner

name: Store submission preparation (mobile)
steps: 1 Prepare metadata and review notes. 2 Check privacy labels. 3 Leave the submission for a human
verification: Package lists each required field

name: Code signing and secrets management (mobile)
steps: 1 List needed signing items. 2 Store them as CI secrets. 3 Write no key to the repo
verification: No key file appears in the repo

name: OTA update configuration (mobile)
steps: 1 Write the rule for what may ship OTA. 2 Write the config with secret references
verification: Rule lists each allowed change type

name: Dependency update automation
steps: 1 Write the update bot config. 2 Set the schedule as PROPOSED
verification: Config validates

name: Performance review
steps: 1 Find re-renders, unvirtualised lists and blocking work. 2 List each with its file
verification: Each finding cites a file

name: Source traceability check
input: Any output file and its source IDs
steps: 1 Check each item cites an input ID, file or line. 2 Flag each item with no source as TBD
verification: Zero untraced items, or each is flagged

name: Assumption and checkpoint log
input: Any gap in a source file
steps: 1 Record the gap with the file and line. 2 List two or more options. 3 Send to A1.05 as a checkpoint. 4 Never choose a default
verification: Each entry has two or more options or says TBD

name: Decision request (human)
steps: 1 Write each option with its trade-off. 2 Give the PROPOSED default and reason. 3 Stop until a named person decides
output: Decision request in a checkpoint file
verification: Request names who decides and what file they read

name: Independent output verification
input: An output file and the input it used
steps: 1 Open a new chat with no prior context. 2 Compare the output with the input. 3 Mark each item PASS or FAIL with the reason. 4 Do not fix anything
verification: Every item has PASS or FAIL

name: Documentation writing (templates)
steps: 1 Pick the template. 2 Fill each field from a source. 3 Write TBD for each gap. 4 Do not add fields the template lacks
save_path: as set by the calling skill
verification: Every field has a source or TBD

name: Git operations
steps: 1 Create the branch named <type>/<task-ID>. 2 Commit with a conventional message. 3 Open the PR. 4 Read CI status. Only A1 commits docs/sdlc/kanban.md
output: Branch, commit, PR link, CI status
verification: CI status is recorded in the handoff file

name: Task gate (lint, types, unit tests) and commit
steps: 1 Run lint. 2 Run the type check. 3 Run the unit tests. 4 Commit only if all three pass
verification: All three results are recorded as pass

name: Pull request creation
steps: 1 Write the summary, test notes and linked task ID. 2 Attach the task gate result. 3 Open the PR
verification: CI is green before review starts

name: Bug fixing
steps: 1 Reproduce the failure. 2 Find the root cause. 3 Apply a minimal fix. 4 Add a test that fails before and passes after
verification: The new test fails before the fix and passes after

name: Minimum UI/UX checklist
steps: 1 Check one primary action per screen. 2 Check loading, empty, error, offline and permission states. 3 Check labels, touch targets (44 pt iOS, 48 dp Android, 24 CSS px web), contrast 4.5:1, text scaling, feedback. 4 Record pass or fail per item
verification: Every item has pass or fail with evidence

name: Secure coding baseline
